A security pass on online play, the relay looking after itself, and what friends are playing on. Relay 1.5.0 goes with it.

**Safer online play (relay 1.5.0, after a security audit)**
- The relay can't be knocked over by one person any more:
  - what waits for each connection is limited in size, and the relay's memory as a whole is kept well inside its limit;
  - connections count from the moment they open, not from their first message;
  - subscribing costs from the same allowance as talking, and a flood of small packets gets a connection disconnected;
  - many messages arriving together are read quickly.
- Nobody can list the topics in use any more, so a private village, a mailbox or a linked device can only be reached by those who know its code.
- Only the kinds of message the game keeps are kept, each address has a limited share, and the relay's own settings (the public list, the squares, what the host keeps open) can't be pushed out.
- A village's listing can only be changed by the player whose it is.
- In the villages the relay's host keeps, the relay tells the host which connection sent each message. Nobody can speak as somebody else there, and the console's mute, ban and block act on the connection that really said it.
- A player can no longer take over a public square by claiming the relay host's id, and the relay's host is believed only on its own channel.
- A banned private village's code is no longer sent out; only a one-way number made from it is.

**The admin console**
- With `ACCESS_TEAM` and `ACCESS_AUD` set, it checks Cloudflare Access's signed sign-in token, not just its email header.
- Its page runs no script but its own, can't be framed, and refuses changes from other sites.
- Reached over an SSH tunnel (`ADMIN_OPEN=1`), it answers only requests addressed to localhost.
- New: players online and what they're on (🐧 🪟 🤖 🌐), and in the list of connections, the name of whoever's in a village the host keeps.
- Players in the host's villages are matched to their connection. A report from an older host is marked as matched only by the id the player gave.
- "Forget them" no longer forgets the relay's own settings.

**Looking after itself**
- With the updater on, it updates the relay and its host every day at a quiet hour (only when there's something newer), clears away old images, and starts the relay again if it stops answering.
- Every container's log is kept small, and [DEPLOY.md](https://github.com/dash1101/xmas-tui/blob/main/relay/DEPLOY.md) covers coming back after a reboot and keeping the machine's own packages up to date.

**Friends**
- Friends & chats shows what each friend is playing on (Windows, Linux, a phone, a browser), once both are on 1.25.3.

**Privacy**
- [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/dash1101/xmas-tui/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) covers what's playing on what, and what the console shows beside each connection.
